title: Same chance, new choice (2:1)
hookLine: complete return: meeting the same situation, able to do it again, and choosing not to
tomorrow: so what are the steps before the chance comes back?

cards: Same group chat. Same person posting the same thing that set you off last time. Your thumbs already know the reply.
You said sorry for that reply, and meant it. So how would you ever know you've really changed? Maimonides says you find out right here.
Not in the apology. In the moment the old chance comes back, exactly the same, and you could do it again.

teach.b: Here's chapter two, the first law, in plain words. What is complete return?
When the chance to do the same wrong comes to a person again, and they're able to do it, and they hold back, because they've returned. Not out of fear, and not because they've grown too weak.
Maimonides makes it vivid: the same person, the same place, the same strength, the same pull. Everything lined up like before. And this time, a different choice.

If someone only returns late, when they can no longer do the old thing anyway, it still counts. They're still one who has returned, even if it isn't called complete. So the apology is real, and so is the late return.

But the proof lives in a moment you can't schedule. Something to tell a friend tonight: in this law, the test of change isn't avoiding the old situation. It's meeting it, fully able, and choosing new.

how: Hilchot Teshuvah 2:1 is studied and quoted in the season before Yom Kippur; its 'same situation, same strength' test is how Maimonides defines complete return (teshuvah gemurah).

o: a lucky break that lets you skip the hard part
a second chance someone gives you to apologize
the old situation comes back, and you choose new

games.q: Maimonides on complete return — tap the pairs.
p: the same chance, and a new choice

s: for Maimonides, the surest proof of change is avoiding the old situation forever
complete return is meeting the same chance, able to do it, and choosing not to.
someone who returns only when they can't do the old thing anymore still counts
they're still one who has returned, even if it isn't called complete.

games.q: your friend quit vaping, then left every party early for a month. tonight she stays, someone offers, and she says no. what would Maimonides call tonight?
o: the real test: the same chance, able to do it, and a new choice.
a risk she should have avoided, since staying away is the goal.
nothing special: she already decided weeks ago, so it was over then.
games.why: Hilchot Teshuvah 2:1: complete return is when the chance comes again, the person could do it, and holds back.

practice: Sit with your hands open on your knees. Picture where an old habit of yours usually shows up: the place, the person, the hour. See yourself there, fully able to do the old thing, and let your open hands choose something else.

wordCard.voice: Same chance. Maimonides' test of complete return: the old situation, the old strength, and a new choice.

orig.note: Hebrew: complete return. Maimonides' term in Hilchot Teshuvah 2:1.

carryVoice: Pocket line: same chance, new choice, and the moment you can't schedule. Three of thirty.

sources.ref: Maimonides, Mishneh Torah, Hilchot Teshuvah 2:1 (complete teshuvah: the same opportunity, the ability, holding back because of teshuvah and not from fear or weakness; the case of the same person, place and strength; a late return still counts)
